sample_size.excerpt: We conducted a population-based prospective study in 43,435 Japanese men aged 45-74 y. Participants responded to a validated questionnaire, which included 138 food items.

cases.excerpt: During the 11.6-y follow-up, of the 825 men newly diagnosed with prostate cancer, 213 had advanced-stage cancer, 582 had organ-localized disease, and 30 had an undetermined stage of disease.

effect_size.excerpt: Total fiber was not associated with total or advanced prostate cancer, with respective multivariable HRs for the highest and lowest quartiles of 1.00 (95% CI: 0.77, 1.29; P-trend = 0.97) and 0.67 (95% CI: 0.42, 1.07; P-trend = 0.30). Total fiber and insoluble fiber intake were associated with a decreased risk of advanced cancers detected by subjective symptoms, with multivariate HRs (95% CIs) across increasing quartiles of 1.00, 0.58, 0.62, and 0.44 (0.21, 0.92; P-trend = 0.05) for total fiber and 1.00, 0.60, 0.52, and 0.46 (0.22, 0.93; P-trend = 0.04) for insoluble fiber.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Total fiber was not associated with total or advanced prostate cancer, with respective multivariable HRs for the highest and lowest quartiles of 1.00 (95% CI: 0.77, 1.29; P-trend = 0.97) and 0.67 (95% CI: 0.42, 1.07; P-trend = 0.30). Total fiber and insoluble fiber intake were associated with a decreased risk of advanced cancers detected by subjective symptoms, with multivariate HRs (95% CIs) across increasing quartiles of 1.00, 0.58, 0.62, and 0.44 (0.21, 0.92; P-trend = 0.05) for total fiber and 1.00, 0.60, 0.52, and 0.46 (0.22, 0.93; P-trend = 0.04) for insoluble fiber.

sample_size.excerpt: We used data from 159,482 participants in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study to investigate associations for recalled adolescent intake of red meat (unprocessed beef and processed red meat), poultry, egg, canned tuna, animal fat and animal protein at ages 12-13 years with subsequent PCa risk and mortality over 14 years of follow-up. Cox proportional hazard regression was used to calculate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of total (n = 17,349), advanced (n = 2,297) and fatal (n = 804) PCa.

cases.excerpt: Cox proportional hazard regression was used to calculate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of total (n = 17,349), advanced (n = 2,297) and fatal (n = 804) PCa.

effect_size.excerpt: In analyses stratified by the number of PSA tests before baseline, trends for unprocessed beef intake were slightly, but not statistically significantly stronger among lesser screened men (0 PSA tests: multivariable-adjusted HR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.72–1.03, P -trend = 0.11; 1 PSA test: HR = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.72–0.99, P -trend = 0.04) and weaker among more heavily screened men (≥2 PSA tests: HR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.84–1.04, P -trend = 0.21; P -interaction = 0.36, comparing ≥2 to 0 PSA tests), whereas no differences in patterns were observed for egg intake.

sample_size.excerpt: Using data from 164,079 men in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study, we performed factor analysis to identify dietary patterns at ages 12-13 years and then used Cox proportional hazards regression to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of total (n = 17,861), non-advanced (n = 15,499), advanced (n = 2362), and fatal PCa (n = 832).

cases.excerpt: Although adolescent diet has been proposed to contribute to prostate cancer (PCa) development, no studies have investigated the relation between adolescent dietary patterns and PCa risk or mortality. Using data from 164,079 men in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study, we performed factor analysis to identify dietary patterns at ages 12-13 years and then used Cox proportional hazards regression to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of total (n = 17,861), non-advanced (n = 15,499), advanced (n = 2362), and fatal PCa (n = 832).

effect_size.excerpt: Although not entirely consistent across analyses, a higher adolescent plant-based pattern (characterised by vegetables, fruits, and dark bread) score was associated with slightly reduced risks of total (fully adjusted HR<sub>Q5vs.Q1</sub> = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.89-0.98, p trend=0.003) and non-advanced PCa (HR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.87-0.96, p trend<0.001), whereas no associations were observed for advanced or fatal PCa, or for Western modern (characterised by sweets, processed meat, beef, cheese, and pizza) or Western traditional (characterised gravy, eggs, potatoes and white bread) patterns. We found evidence to support a modest, protective role for a plant-based dietary pattern during adolescence on PCa risk.

continent.excerpt: Baseline questionnaires were mailed to AARP members 50–70 years of age residing in six states (California, Florida, Louisiana, New Jersey, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania) and two metropolitan areas (Atlanta and Detroit).

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Adolescent diet was assessed by a 37-item food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) included on the supplemental risk factor questionnaire.

results.title: Higher insoluble fiber intake is associated with a lower risk of prostate cancer: results from the PLCO cohort.
results.reason: This prospective PLCO cohort study evaluates dietary insoluble fiber intake in relation to incident prostate cancer and provides an adjusted hazard ratio, confidence interval, and p-value.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest quartile (Q4) versus lowest quartile (Q1) of insoluble fiber intake
extraction.timing: Prospective dietary assessment and follow-up for incident prostate cancer
extraction.population: Men aged 55–74 years enrolled in the PLCO cohort

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 54,336 participants in the United States, consisting of 6,414 patients with PCa, were included in this study.

cases.excerpt: Therefore, this study examined the relationship between fiber intake and the risk of PCa by using data from Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial. A total of 54,336 participants in the United States, consisting of 6,414 patients with PCa, were included in this study.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quartile, individuals in the highest quartile of insoluble fiber intake had a significantly lower risk of PCa (aHR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78-0.98). By contrast, no significant associations were detected between total fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80-1.01) or soluble fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80-1.02).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quartile, individuals in the highest quartile of insoluble fiber intake had a significantly lower risk of PCa (aHR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78-0.98).

p_value.excerpt: As shown in Table 2 , compared with those of subjects in the lowest quartile of insoluble fiber (Q1), the aHRs of PCa risk were 0.97 (95% CI, 0.90–1.05; P = 0.453), 0.97 (95% CI, 0.90–1.06; P = 0.526), and 0.87 (95% CI, 0.78–0.98; P = 0.016) for groups Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively.

extraction.timing: Dietary History Questionnaire completion at baseline; incident prostate cancer follow-up through 31 December 2009
extraction.population: Men aged 55–74 years participating in the PLCO Cancer Screening Trial

sample_size.excerpt: This prospective cohort included 49,424 men from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial.

cases.excerpt: During follow-up, we documented 4,308 incident cases of PCa, of whom 392 died from PCa.

effect_size.excerpt: As Supplementary Table S7 shows, after full adjustment for potential confounders including demographic characteristics and key dietary nutrients (model 3), higher dietary total fat, SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs, and trans-fat acids intake were not associated with the incidence of PCa, with the HRs Q4vs.Q1 (95%CIs) for overall PCa incidence being 1.09 (0.93–1.28), 0.95 (0.82–1.10), 1.03 (0.92–1.15), 1.12 (0.98–1.27), and 0.95 (0.86–1.06), respectively (all P for trend >0.05). sample_size.excerpt: The association between 21 vegetables and eight fruits and prostate cancer risk was assessed in the Netherlands Cohort Study among 58,279 men of ages 55-69 years at baseline in 1986. After 6.3 years of follow-up, 610 cases with complete vegetable data and 642 cases with complete fruit data were available for analysis.

cases.excerpt: After 6.3 years of follow-up, 610 cases with complete vegetable data and 642 cases with complete fruit data were available for analysis.

effect_size.excerpt: Observed positive associations were significant for consumption of leek (RR, 1.38) and oranges (RR, 1.07) and nonsignificant for sweet peppers (RR, 1.60) and mushrooms (RR, 1.49). Results in subgroups of cases were more or less consistent with the overall results.
